item.title: REFLECTION: The Rev. Jesse Jackson's fight for justice included Chicago grocery store aisles • The TRiiBE
item.description: Rev. Jesse Jackson believed that Black communities had to control the local economy, demanding that grocers provide adequate produce and meat, supply jobs for Black people, and carry Black products.

item.title: Alders reject proposal to fine parents if their children violate curfew, drag race • The TRiiBE
item.description: Ald. Raymond Lopez, the proposal’s sponsor, said the goal is not to criminalize parents: “If they are not or if they are knowingly dismissing what their children are up to, then they should be held accountable, plain and simple."

item.title: IL 07 candidates describe plans to address affordable housing, child care and health care during West Side forum • The TRiiBE
item.description: Democratic candidates in the Illinois 7th Congressional race answered questions raised by grassroots and community-based organizations during a Feb. 12 forum hosted by the Chicago Black Voter Project.

item.title: Woodlawn tenants fear displacement months before opening of Obama Center • The TRiiBE
item.description: Organizers say a prospective buyer is planning to raise rents at affordable housing property.

item.title: ‘This is not a homegoing — this is a celebration,’ thousands gather at South Side church to honor the Rev. Jesse Louis Jackson • The TRiiBE
item.description: At a five-hour service in the Pullman community, presidents, preachers and ordinary people gathered to celebrate a man who told generations of Black Americans they were somebody worth fighting for.

item.title: Legacy Awards celebrates 10 years of supporting emerging business leaders with its Young Entrepreneur of the Year Award • The TRiiBE
item.description: Meet this year's finalists competing for the award as they continue their missions of long-lasting impact.

item.title: Omega Psi Phi fraternity hosting community blood drive on Chicago’s South Side • The TRiiBE
item.description: The Omicron Mu Mu graduate chapter is calling on community members to donate blood March 22 as part of the fraternity’s long-running service tradition inspired by pioneering physician and Omega Psi Phi member Charles R. Drew.

item.title: LETTER: Chicago, we must end pretextual stops • The TRiiBE
item.description: March 21 marked the two-year anniversary of Dexter Reed’s death. Pretextual stops are still rampant across Chicago.

item.title: Red Clay Dance Company’s La Femme Festival centers Black women choreographers • The TRiiBE
item.description: The biennial Women’s History Month event returns March 27–28 with masterclasses, performances, and conversations celebrating the work of women in dance.

item.title: OPINION: What Black students actually need to succeed in college • The TRiiBE
item.description: Black students are not failing college. In too many cases, college is failing them.
